### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

I suggest revisiting `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt/default.txt` and simplifying it substantially, using the newer `gpt-astra.txt` as a reference for the general style and level of detail.

The current fallback prompt appears to have accumulated a large number of very specific instructions over time. It is currently about twice the size of `gpt-astra.txt` and contains many low-level or repetitive directives, for example:

* several repeated instructions to keep responses extremely short, including multiple examples
* a hard limit of fewer than four lines of text
* detailed rules about how to batch shell/tool calls
* a blanket prohibition on adding comments unless explicitly asked
* mandatory lint/typecheck behavior
* detailed instructions about which search tool to prefer
* CLI-specific presentation assumptions
* detailed instructions for questions about OpenCode itself

Some of these may still be useful, but modern capable models generally need much less procedural prompting than older models did. A long list of narrowly specified rules also makes the fallback harder to maintain and more likely to contain outdated, redundant, or mutually awkward instructions.

This matters particularly because `default.txt` is not merely a legacy fallback for weak or unusual models. Current strong models without a dedicated prompt, such as GLM 5.3 / GLM 5.3 Flash and MiMo V2.6 Pro, also receive it.

### Suggested direction

I would suggest refactoring `default.txt` toward the style of `gpt-astra.txt`, without necessarily copying that prompt verbatim.

`gpt-astra.txt` seems to capture most of the important harness-level behavior much more compactly:

* concise communication
* appropriate autonomy
* parallel tool use where useful
* preference for dedicated tools over shell commands
* sensible handling of ongoing work and user steering
* consistency with an existing codebase
* appropriate verification/testing
* respect for user work
* clear rules around delegation

I propose keeping this scoped to `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt/default.txt`, the fallback system prompt, rather than adding a new mode or changing provider-specific prompts.

The current fallback repeats its brevity rules and combines a hard four-line/one-word target with instructions to explain non-trivial commands. It also tells the agent to stop after editing a file, which can cut off validation or other work needed to complete an action request. I would consolidate communication into one section that scales detail to the task, and make an action request carry through implementation and the relevant checks. The model-neutral layout of the newer prompt is a useful reference; model-specific wording would stay out of the fallback.
